quotes.quote: Beyond public benchmarks, we introduce Z.ai Code Bench, an in-house benchmark designed to evaluate coding agents under realistic user scenarios.
It covers diverse task categories and places agents in complex local development environments.
At different effort levels, we evaluate agents along two dimensions: end-to-end task completion rate and fine-grained checklist accuracy.
As a private benchmark, Z.ai Code Bench also reduces the risk of contamination from public test sets and gives us a more faithful measure of real-world user experience.
It delivers markedly stronger agentic coding results than GLM-5.2 at every effort level while consuming fewer output tokens.
At Max effort, GLM-5.3 reaches 34.5% at roughly 75K output tokens per task, compared with 23.4% at 96K for GLM-5.2.
At High effort, GLM-5.3 reaches 31.4% at around 50K output tokens, surpassing Claude Opus 4.8 at 29.5% with 120K.
GLM-5.3 remains behind Claude Fable 5, which reaches 39.5% at Max effort.
For GLM-5.3, we pushed environment scaling toward tasks that look less like coding exercises and more like real units of expert work.
It uses the same base model as GLM-5.2, with all improvements driven by post-training.
GLM-5.3 delivers a significant improvement in coding capabilities, achieving a 50% performance gain over GLM-5.2 on Z.ai Code Bench.
GLM-5.3 always operates with reasoning enabled and supports three reasoning effort levels
Disabling reasoning is no longer supported.
for complex tasks such as coding, we recommend using max

This holds on our in-house coding evaluation as well: on Z.ai Code Bench v1.0 (run on Claude Code 2.1.207), GLM-5.3-Flash clearly outperforms GLM-5.2 at every effort level, and at max effort nearly matches Claude Opus 4.8 (29.0 vs. 29.5).
GLM-5: from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering
We present GLM-5, a next-generation foundation model designed to transition the paradigm of vibe coding to agentic engineering.
(For the complete list of authors, please refer to the Contribution section)

We upgraded our internal CC-Bench to CC-Bench-V2 to evaluate whether the model can correctly complete end-to-end tasks in realistic agentic engineering environments across frontend, backend, and long-horizon tasks.
CC-Bench-V2 removes human labeling entirely and is fully automated via Claude Code and other agent harnesses with unit tests and Agent-as-a-Judge techniques.
We curate 85 tasks spanning six languages (Python, Go, C++, Rust, Java, and TypeScript)
We report Pass@1, where a task is considered solved only if all its associated unit tests pass.
Real-world experience matters more than leaderboards.
Terminal-Bench 2.1: We evaluate in Claude Code 2.1.207 with temperature=1.0, top_p=1, max_new_tokens=65536 with 6h timeout.
